name: Urinary system
description: The kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra: where they lie, how the nephron filters the blood and makes urine, the hormones that control it, and common disorders. Picture questions show the organs, drawn see-through inside the lower trunk, with one part highlighted to name.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: What are the organs of the urinary system?
answers: Two kidneys, two ureters, the bladder and the urethra
wrong: Kidneys, adrenal glands, bladder and urethra
questions.explanation: The kidneys make urine; the rest store it and carry it out.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a main function of the kidneys?
wrong: Balancing the blood's salts and pH
questions.explanation: The liver makes bile. Kidneys also make erythropoietin and renin, and activate vitamin D.

questions.prompt: Which organs are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A pair of bean-shaped organs at the back of the abdomen, either side of the spine.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: About how big is a kidney?
answers: About the size of a fist
wrong: About the size of a golf ball
About the size of a football
questions.explanation: About 11 cm long, 6 cm wide and 3 cm thick, and about 150 g.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with the kidneys in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It sits a little lower than the left kidney, because the liver pushes on it from above.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It lies a little higher than the right, about level with T12 to L3.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: At about which vertebral levels do the kidneys lie?
questions.explanation: The lower ribs partly protect them. The right one lies about a centimetre lower than the left.

questions.prompt: Where are the kidneys in relation to the peritoneum?
questions.explanation: They are held in a cushion of fat, the perirenal fat, and wrapped in renal fascia.

questions.prompt: What is the notch on the inner edge of the kidney, where the vessels and ureter enter and leave, called?
What are the two main layers of the kidney tissue, from outside in?
questions.explanation: The medulla is made of cone-shaped renal pyramids, whose tips (papillae) open into the minor calyces.

questions.prompt: What is the funnel-shaped space inside the kidney that collects urine and drains it into the ureter called?
questions.explanation: The minor calyces join into major calyces, which join into the renal pelvis.

questions.prompt: Which cup-shaped spaces collect urine from the tips of the renal pyramids?
What is the working unit of the kidney called?
questions.explanation: About a million in each kidney.

questions.prompt: What are the main parts of a nephron, in order from the blood?
answers: Renal corpuscle, proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule
Glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule
wrong: Loop of Henle, renal corpuscle, distal tubule, proximal tubule
Proximal tubule, renal corpuscle, distal tubule, loop of Henle
Renal corpuscle, distal tubule, loop of Henle, proximal tubule
questions.explanation: The collecting duct, which several nephrons empty into, is not part of the nephron itself.

questions.prompt: What is the knot of capillaries where blood is filtered in the kidney called?
questions.explanation: It sits inside Bowman's capsule, which collects the filtrate.

questions.prompt: About how much filtrate do the kidneys make each minute (the glomerular filtration rate)?
questions.explanation: That is about 180 litres a day. Only about 1.5 litres leaves as urine, as the rest is reabsorbed.

questions.prompt: About what share of the filtrate is reabsorbed?
questions.explanation: Two thirds of it in the proximal tubule alone.

questions.prompt: In which part of the nephron is most of the filtered water, salt and all the glucose reabsorbed?
questions.explanation: Its cells have a brush border to give a large surface.

questions.prompt: What does the loop of Henle make possible?
questions.explanation: It builds a salt gradient in the medulla, which draws water out of the collecting duct.

questions.prompt: Which hormone makes the collecting ducts more permeable to water, so the urine becomes more concentrated?
questions.explanation: Made by the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: Which hormone from the adrenal cortex makes the kidney keep sodium and lose potassium?
questions.explanation: Water follows the sodium, so blood volume and pressure rise.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme released by the kidney when blood pressure falls starts the renin–angiotensin system?
questions.explanation: From the juxtaglomerular cells.

questions.prompt: Which hormone, made by the kidney in response to low oxygen, makes the bone marrow produce red blood cells?
questions.explanation: People with kidney failure become anaemic because they don't make enough.

questions.prompt: The kidney does the last step of activating which vitamin?
questions.explanation: Into calcitriol, which helps absorb calcium from the gut.

questions.prompt: Which waste, made by the liver from the breakdown of amino acids, is the main nitrogen waste in urine?
Which waste from muscle is used to estimate how well the kidneys are filtering?
questions.explanation: A rising creatinine in the blood means a falling filtration rate.

questions.prompt: What gives urine its yellow colour?
questions.explanation: A product of the breakdown of haemoglobin.

questions.prompt: About how much urine does an adult make each day?
Which disease can cause sugar to spill into the urine, because the filtered glucose is more than the tubules can reabsorb?
questions.explanation: The glucose draws water with it, so the person passes a lot of urine and gets thirsty.

questions.prompt: A lack of ADH makes the kidneys pass large amounts of dilute urine. What is the condition called?
What treatment filters the blood of a person whose kidneys have failed?
questions.explanation: A transplant is the other option. A transplanted kidney is placed in the pelvis, not in the original position.

questions.prompt: What are hard lumps of mineral salts that form in the kidney and can block the ureter, causing severe pain, called?
questions.explanation: The pain (renal colic) goes from the loin down towards the groin.

questions.prompt: What is infection of the kidney, usually spread up from the bladder, called?
What is inflammation of the filtering units of the kidney called?
questions.explanation: Often after an infection, such as a streptococcal throat, or in autoimmune disease.

questions.prompt: About what share of the heart's output goes to the kidneys?
questions.explanation: Although they're less than 1% of body weight.

questions.prompt: Which vessels are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Short, wide branches of the abdominal aorta at about L1 to L2. The right one passes behind the inferior vena cava.

figure.alt: The kidneys and their vessels, with the renal arteries in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which vessels are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: They leave the hilum in front of the arteries and drain into the inferior vena cava. The left one is longer.

figure.alt: The kidneys and their vessels, with the renal veins in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: At the hilum of the kidney, which comes first from front to back?
answers: Renal vein, then renal artery, then renal pelvis (ureter)
questions.explanation: "VAP": vein, artery, pelvis.

questions.prompt: Which glands are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A pair of small glands sitting on top of the kidneys. They belong to the endocrine system, not the urinary system.

figure.alt: The kidneys and adrenal glands, with the adrenal glands in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the two parts of an adrenal gland?
answers: The adrenal cortex and the adrenal medulla
questions.explanation: The cortex makes steroid hormones (cortisol and aldosterone); the medulla makes adrenaline.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with the adrenal glands in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which structures are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Two muscular tubes about 25 cm long, taking urine from the kidneys down to the bladder.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How does urine move down the ureters?
wrong: By the pressure of the blood
questions.explanation: Even when a person is lying down or upside down.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with the ureters in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Where do kidney stones most often get stuck in the ureter?
answers: At the narrow points: where it leaves the kidney, crosses the pelvic brim and enters the bladder
wrong: In the middle of its length
Nowhere: the ureter is wide throughout
questions.explanation: The three narrowings are the pelviureteric junction, the pelvic brim and the vesicoureteric junction.

questions.prompt: In the pelvis, the ureter passes beneath which vessel in women (the 'water under the bridge')?
questions.explanation: A danger in hysterectomy, where the ureter can be cut or tied by mistake. In men it passes under the ductus deferens.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A muscular bag in the pelvis, behind the pubic bones.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with one part in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: About how much urine can the adult bladder hold comfortably?
questions.explanation: The urge to pass urine starts at about 200 to 300 mL.

figure.alt: The kidneys, ureters and bladder inside the lower trunk, with the bladder in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the smooth muscle of the bladder wall called?
questions.explanation: It contracts to empty the bladder.

questions.prompt: What is the smooth triangular area at the base of the bladder, between the two ureters and the urethra, called?
questions.explanation: A common site of infection and stones.

questions.prompt: What are the folds in the lining of an empty bladder called?
questions.explanation: They flatten as the bladder fills.

questions.prompt: Which kind of epithelium lines the bladder and ureters and stretches as they fill?
Which sphincter at the bladder neck is made of smooth muscle and is involuntary?
questions.explanation: In men it also closes to stop semen going back into the bladder.

questions.prompt: Which sphincter, made of skeletal muscle, lets us hold urine voluntarily?
questions.explanation: Supplied by the pudendal nerve.

questions.prompt: Which part of the nervous system's outflow makes the bladder contract and empties it?
questions.explanation: Sympathetic nerves relax the detrusor and close the internal sphincter, to let it fill.

questions.prompt: What word do we use for the passing of urine?
How does the urethra differ between men and women?
answers: It is about 20 cm long in men and about 4 cm in women
Longer in men, shorter in women
wrong: It is the same length in both
questions.explanation: The short female urethra is why women get bladder infections more often.

questions.prompt: What is the inflammation of the bladder, usually from infection, called?
questions.explanation: Most often from bacteria (usually E. coli) from the bowel.

questions.prompt: What is the accidental loss of urine called?
What is a tube passed through the urethra to drain the bladder called?
What is a urine output below about 400 mL a day called?
questions.explanation: Anuria is almost none; polyuria is too much.

questions.prompt: Which gland surrounds the first part of the male urethra, and can squeeze it when it enlarges?
questions.explanation: Benign enlargement of the prostate makes older men pass urine slowly and often.
